speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; since you are a newborn, I need to know how many hours old you are and whether you have been feeding well. Can you tell me if your stool color is normal or if it has become pale or clay-colored? Also, have you noticed any fever or excessive sleepiness?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; since the infant is exclusively breastfed and gaining weight appropriately, we need to rule out biliary atresia or hemolysis. Have you noticed if the stools have turned pale or clay-colored, and is the urine very dark? Also, has any blood type incompatibility been mentioned in your pregnancy records?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Biliary Atresia. Given the 2-week-old age, exclusively breastfed status with weight gain, and the critical family history of a sibling requiring liver surgery, I am requesting immediate confirmation via ultrasound and liver biopsy. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Liver Biopsy and Direct Bilirubin levels.
